finding.claim: The /fetch handler passes the user-supplied `target` query parameter straight to http.Get. An attacker can make the server request arbitrary URLs, such as cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254), localhost services and internal hosts. The response body is copied back to the caller, so this is a full-read SSRF.
finding.source: r.URL.Query().Get("target") (main.go:15), reached via the HTTP route /fetch
finding.sink: http.Get(target) (main.go:16), with the response body written back via io.Copy(w, resp.Body) (main.go:22)

trace.note: target is read from the query string without modification
The response body is returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: None. There is no scheme check, no host allowlist, no IP or private-range blocking, and no redirect restriction. The allowlist (`allowed`) is only used in safeFetch, not here.

verdict.reason: main.go:15-16 passes the unauthenticated query param `target` directly to http.Get, with no middleware or validation (the `allowed` check exists only in safeFetch at main.go:27), and main.go:22 copies the response body back to the caller.
